public_rationale: The first part holds. In fiscal 2025, NVIDIA's Data Center revenue was $115.2 billion of $130.5 billion, about 88%, so it made most of its money selling data center chips to other companies. The second part says buyers mainly purchase GPUs so they can lose money selling software. That cannot be measured. Some buyers, such as OpenAI, were losing billions. But NVIDIA's largest buyers are big cloud and platform companies that rent compute or use it internally, and none report AI-specific profit or loss. 'Our economy is held up by NVIDIA' is rhetoric and is not scored. With one part supported and the distinctive part untestable, the claim stays unresolved.
limitations: Data Center revenue includes networking, not only GPUs.
Results come from a reprint of NVIDIA's release, because the primary pages could not be read.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: NVIDIA props up the economy by selling GPUs mostly to companies that lose money on AI software.

our_interpretation: Element 1: more than half of NVIDIA's revenue comes from selling data center GPUs and systems to other companies. Checkable from company results.

Element 2: the main purpose of those buyers' GPU purchases is to sell AI software that currently loses money. This needs evidence on what the main buyers use GPUs for and whether those uses lose money.
'Our economy is held up by NVIDIA' is treated as rhetorical framing and not scored.
Ongoing state with no named period: use NVIDIA's latest full fiscal year reported before the post, fiscal 2025 (ended 2025-01-26, reported 2025-02-26).
criteria.support_condition: NVIDIA data shows most revenue comes from data center sales, and evidence shows its main buyers mostly use the GPUs to run loss-making AI software businesses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Data center sales are not most of NVIDIA's revenue. Or the main buyers mostly use the GPUs for profitable purposes, such as profitable cloud rental or internal workloads like ad ranking, rather than loss-making software.
